## Naive Bayes models

```{r section_1, echo=TRUE}
# Models:
#   1. Macroeconomic indicators only
#   2. Macroeconomic + financial indicators
# Forecast horizons: 3, 6, 12 months
# Evaluation metrics: AUC and F1 Score
```

## Configuration

```{r section_3, echo=TRUE}

HORIZONS <- c(3, 6, 12)

# Chronological split:
# Initial training target dates: before January 1980
# Validation target dates: January 1980 - December 1985
# Final model training target dates: before January 1986
# OOS forecast origins: January 1986 onward
# Four episodes before 1986, four from 1986 onward.

VALIDATION_START <- as.Date("1980-01-01")
TEST_START <- as.Date("1986-01-01")

# Numerical stabilization for Gaussian Naive Bayes
# To control for numerical instability if variance of predictor within a class is too small
NB_EPSILON <- 1e-6

# Main classification threshold (fixed baseline)
FIXED_THRESHOLD <- 0.50

# Candidate thresholds for validation-only robustness analysis
THRESHOLD_GRID <- seq(
  0.05,
  0.95,
  by = 0.01
)
```

## Load Data

```{r section_4, echo=TRUE}
# Load datasets directly
macro_data <- read_csv(
  "../data/processed/fred_md_macro_clean_final.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

full_data <- read_csv(
  "../data/processed/fred_md_macro_financial_clean_final.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

# Ensure dates are correctly formatted
macro_data <- macro_data %>%
  mutate(sasdate = as.Date(sasdate))

full_data <- full_data %>%
  mutate(sasdate = as.Date(sasdate))

# Identify predictors
macro_predictors <- setdiff(
  names(macro_data),
  c("sasdate", "USREC")
)

full_predictors <- setdiff(
  names(full_data),
  c("sasdate", "USREC")
)

financial_predictors <- setdiff(
  full_predictors,
  macro_predictors
)

# Validate predictors
if (!all(macro_predictors %in% full_predictors)) {
  stop("Some macro predictors are absent from full dataset.")
}

# Display predictor counts

cat("\nNumber of macro predictors:",
    length(macro_predictors))

cat("\nNumber of financial predictors:",
    length(financial_predictors))

cat("\nTotal predictors in full model:",
    length(full_predictors), "\n")
```

## Create Forecast Target

```{r section_5, echo=TRUE}
# Y_t^(h) = USREC_(t+h)
# Predict recession status exactly h months ahead.

create_target <- function(df, horizon) {
  
  df %>%
    mutate(
      target = lead(USREC, horizon),
      target_date = sasdate %m+% months(horizon)
    ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(target))
}
```

## Evaluation Metrics: F1 And Auc

```{r section_6, echo=TRUE}
calculate_metrics <- function(
    actual,
    probability,
    threshold = 0.5
) {
  
  predicted <- as.integer(
    probability >= threshold
  )
  
  TP <- sum(predicted == 1 & actual == 1)
  FP <- sum(predicted == 1 & actual == 0)
  FN <- sum(predicted == 0 & actual == 1)
  
  # F1 Score
  denominator <- 2 * TP + FP + FN
  
  f1 <- if (denominator == 0) {
    0
  } else {
    2 * TP / denominator
  }
  
  # AUC
  auc_value <- if (
    length(unique(actual)) == 2
  ) {
    
    roc_obj <- pROC::roc(
      response = actual,
      predictor = probability,
      levels = c(0, 1),
      direction = "<",
      quiet = TRUE
    )
    
    as.numeric(
      pROC::auc(roc_obj)
    )
    
  } else {
    NA_real_
  }
  
  data.frame(
    AUC = auc_value,
    F1 = f1
  )
}
```

## Robustness Check: Validation-Optimized Threshold

```{r section_7, echo=TRUE}
# Main results use FIXED_THRESHOLD = 0.50.
# This alternative threshold is selected using validation F1 only.
# OOS test observations are not used to select thresholds.

optimize_threshold <- function(
    actual,
    probability
) {
  
  scores <- sapply(
    THRESHOLD_GRID,
    function(th) {
      
      calculate_metrics(
        actual = actual,
        probability = probability,
        threshold = th
      )$F1
    }
  )
  
  # If multiple thresholds tie, select the one
  # closest to 0.5.
  
  best <- which(
    scores == max(scores, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
  
  best <- best[
    which.min(
      abs(THRESHOLD_GRID[best] - 0.5)
    )
  ]
  
  return(THRESHOLD_GRID[best])
}
```

## Fit Gaussian Naive Bayes

```{r section_8, echo=TRUE}
fit_nb_model <- function(train, predictors) {
  
  x_train <- train[, predictors, drop = FALSE]
  
  # Keep predictors with sufficient finite observations
  valid_vars <- predictors[
    sapply(x_train, function(x) {
      observed <- x[is.finite(x)]
      length(observed) >= 2 &&
        length(unique(observed)) > 1
    })
  ]
  
  if (length(valid_vars) == 0) {
    stop("No usable predictors.")
  }
  
  x_train <- x_train[, valid_vars, drop = FALSE]
  
  # Calculate medians using training data only
  medians <- sapply(x_train, function(x) {
    median(x[is.finite(x)])
  })
  
  # Replace missing values with training medians
  for (v in valid_vars) {
    x_train[[v]][!is.finite(x_train[[v]])] <- medians[[v]]
  }
  
  x_train$target <- factor(
    train$target,
    levels = c(0, 1)
  )
  
  if (length(unique(train$target)) < 2) {
    stop("Training data must contain both classes.")
  }
  
  model <- e1071::naiveBayes(
    target ~ .,
    data = x_train,
    laplace = 1,
    threshold = NB_EPSILON,
    eps = NB_EPSILON
  )
  
  list(
    model = model,
    variables = valid_vars,
    medians = medians
  )
}

predict_nb <- function(fitted, newdata) {
  
  x <- newdata[
    , fitted$variables,
    drop = FALSE
  ]
  
  # Replace missing values using TRAINING medians (Prevent Data Leakage)
  for (v in fitted$variables) {
    x[[v]][!is.finite(x[[v]])] <- fitted$medians[[v]]
  }
  
  prob <- predict(
    fitted$model,
    newdata = x,
    type = "raw"
  )
  
  as.numeric(prob[, "1"])
}
```

## Train And Evaluate One Model

```{r section_9, echo=TRUE}
run_nb <- function(
    df,
    horizon,
    model_name
) {
  
  data_h <- create_target(
    df,
    horizon
  )
  
  predictors <- setdiff(
    names(df),
    c("sasdate", "USREC")
  )
  
  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # A. INITIAL TRAINING / VALIDATION
  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  
  train <- data_h %>%
    filter(
      target_date < VALIDATION_START
    )
  
  validation <- data_h %>%
    filter(
      target_date >= VALIDATION_START,
      target_date < TEST_START
    )
  
  if (
    nrow(train) == 0 ||
    nrow(validation) == 0
  ) {
    stop("Training or validation sample is empty.")
  }
  
  # Fit model on initial training data
  initial_fit <- fit_nb_model(
    train,
    predictors
  )
  
  # Validation probabilities
  val_prob <- predict_nb(
    initial_fit,
    validation
  )
  
  # Optimize F1 classification threshold
  best_threshold <- optimize_threshold(
    validation$target,
    val_prob
  )
  
  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # B. REFIT USING ALL PRE-OOS OBSERVATIONS
  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  
  final_train <- data_h %>%
    filter(
      target_date < TEST_START
    )
  
  final_fit <- fit_nb_model(
    final_train,
    predictors
  )
  
  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # C. OUT-OF-SAMPLE TESTING
  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  
  test <- data_h %>%
    filter(
      sasdate >= TEST_START
    )
  
  if (nrow(test) == 0) {
    stop("OOS test sample is empty.")
  }
  
  # All final training targets end before the first test forecast origin.
  stopifnot(max(final_train$target_date) < min(test$sasdate))
  
  # Predict OOS probabilities
  test_prob <- predict_nb(
    final_fit,
    test
  )
  
  # Main test predictions: fixed 0.50 threshold
  test_pred <- as.integer(test_prob >= FIXED_THRESHOLD)
  
  # Primary evaluation: fixed-threshold F1 and threshold-independent AUC
  metrics <- calculate_metrics(
    actual = test$target,
    probability = test_prob,
    threshold = FIXED_THRESHOLD
  )
  
  # Robustness check: validation-optimized threshold applied unchanged to test
  robustness_metrics <- calculate_metrics(
    actual = test$target,
    probability = test_prob,
    threshold = best_threshold
  )
  
  metrics$Horizon <- horizon
  metrics$Model <- model_name
  metrics$Threshold <- FIXED_THRESHOLD
  metrics$Optimized_Threshold <- best_threshold
  metrics$F1_Optimized <- robustness_metrics$F1
  metrics$Delta_F1_Optimized_vs_Fixed <- robustness_metrics$F1 - metrics$F1
  metrics$Train_N <- nrow(final_train)
  metrics$Validation_N <- nrow(validation)
  metrics$Test_N <- nrow(test)
  metrics$Predictors <- length(
    final_fit$variables
  )
  
  predictions <- data.frame(
    date = test$sasdate,
    target_date = test$target_date,
    actual = test$target,
    probability = test_prob,
    predicted = test_pred,
    horizon = horizon,
    model = model_name
  )
  
  list(
    model = final_fit$model,
    variables = final_fit$variables,
    medians = final_fit$medians,
    metrics = metrics,
    predictions = predictions,
    validation_threshold = best_threshold
  )
}
```

## Train All Six Models

```{r section_10, echo=TRUE}
results <- list()

for (h in HORIZONS) {
  
  # Model 1: Macroeconomic indicators only
  results[[paste0("Macro_", h)]] <- run_nb(
    macro_data,
    horizon = h,
    model_name = "Macro"
  )
  
  # Model 2: Macroeconomic + financial indicators
  results[[paste0("Full_", h)]] <- run_nb(
    full_data,
    horizon = h,
    model_name = "Macro + Financial"
  )
}
```

## Combine Model Results

```{r section_11, echo=TRUE}
metrics_table <- bind_rows(
  lapply(results, function(x) x$metrics)
) %>%
  select(
    Horizon,
    Model,
    Predictors,
    Train_N,
    Validation_N,
    Test_N,
    Threshold,
    AUC,
    F1,
    Optimized_Threshold,
    F1_Optimized,
    Delta_F1_Optimized_vs_Fixed
  ) %>%
  arrange(Horizon, Model)
```

## Incremental Value Of Financial Indicators

```{r section_12, echo=TRUE}
comparison <- metrics_table %>%
  select(Horizon, Model, AUC, F1) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Model,
    values_from = c(AUC, F1)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Delta_AUC =
      `AUC_Macro + Financial` - AUC_Macro,
    Delta_F1 =
      `F1_Macro + Financial` - F1_Macro
  ) %>%
  select(Horizon, Delta_AUC, Delta_F1)

# Add incremental value to the main metrics table
metrics_table <- metrics_table %>%
  left_join(comparison, by = "Horizon")

knitr::kable(
  metrics_table,
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Naive Bayes Out-of-Sample Model Performance"
)
```

## Combine Out-Of-Sample Predictions

```{r section_13, echo=TRUE}
predictions_table <- bind_rows(
  lapply(results, function(x) x$predictions)
) %>%
  arrange(horizon, model, date)
```

## Generate Roc Curves

```{r section_14, echo=TRUE}
create_roc_plot <- function(h) {
  
  horizon_data <- predictions_table %>%
    filter(horizon == h)
  
  roc_list <- lapply(
    split(horizon_data, horizon_data$model),
    function(d) {
      pROC::roc(
        response = d$actual,
        predictor = d$probability,
        levels = c(0, 1),
        direction = "<",
        quiet = TRUE
      )
    }
  )
  
  pROC::ggroc(roc_list) +
    geom_abline(
      slope = 1,
      intercept = 0,
      linetype = "dashed",
      color = "grey50"
    ) +
    labs(
      title = paste0(
        "ROC Curve: ",
        h,
        "-Month Recession Forecast"
      ),
      x = "False Positive Rate",
      y = "True Positive Rate",
      color = "Model"
    ) +
    theme_minimal()
}

# Generate and display ROC curves
for (h in HORIZONS) {
  print(create_roc_plot(h))
}
```
